doc.title: Eddie Bert interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Why he ended up in historic situations
summary: Bert credits luck and adapting to each leader's personality.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: What was it about the way you played that you were able to find your way into — I’m not asking this very well, but you’ve participated in what we now consider to be some important, historical situations.
And I’m wondering what was it about your playing or your personality or both that found your way into those things?
I don’t know. Something happened I guess. Lucky I guess.
But you must have had a quick ear and ability to deal with those sometimes chaotic situations — it wasn’t just reading the notes.

Yeah well you have to adapt yourself to what’s going on you know. I guess that’s what it is. Because each band is different. It’s not like that now. Everything is like one level, there’s no waves. But in those days there was all kinds of stuff going on. I mean Mingus had his personality and Monk had his personality, Benny Goodman had his personality, Stan Kenton, Woody. I mean they were all different. So when you joined the band you had to fit in with that situation.
